subject: Visibility gateway runbook and egress checklist — run & review
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
To: ops@logisticscorp.com, cloudops@acme-enterprise.com
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Oct 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Visibility gateway runbook and egress checklist — run & review

Hi all,

Following our kickoff last week, I'm attaching the first-draft runbook for the visibility gateway we'll deploy into LogisticsCorp's VPC (attached: visibility-gateway-runbook.md). The goal for this thread is a focused review of the egress/ingress constraints and logging outputs so we can sign off on the deployment window next week. Specific asks: 

- Ops: confirm you can open the outbound ports below from the app subnets (TCP 443 to Splunk HEC, UDP 514 for syslog if needed) and whether you require a NAT or VPC endpoint.
- Acme cloudops: confirm whether your transit VPC needs a route for the visibility gateway private IPs and if there are peering security group caveats.
- Internal: Laura and Marissa, please review the evidence checklist (SOC2-friendly export, retention policy, and KMS key usage) and add any items to the runbook before I send it to security.

Summary of the proposed pattern in the doc: a small HA cluster (2–3 replicas) running the gateway in a private subnet. The gateway will forward sanitized logs and trace spans to a managed Splunk HEC endpoint over mTLS. We will publish a short IP block for firewall allowlisting (attached csv). The gateway also exposes an internal metrics endpoint (Prometheus format) to CloudWatch/Stackdriver via a sidecar when required.

Timing: propose maintenance window Friday 2028-10-26 23:00–02:00 UTC if the network egress allows it.

Thanks — looking for confirmations and blockers.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.ai

Attachment stubs:
- visibility-gateway-runbook.md (runbook draft, ~8 pages)
- network-egress-ip-list.csv (3 IP ranges)
- splunk-hec-config.yaml (example HEC token + tls config)

From: ops@logisticscorp.com <ops@logisticscorp.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, cloudops@acme-enterprise.com
Date: Thu, 18 Oct 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Visibility gateway runbook and egress checklist — run & review

Jonas,

Thanks for the doc. A couple of immediate notes from our side after a quick pass: 

1) Firewall: we can allow TCP/443 to Splunk HEC but prefer that you hand over a short IP CIDR rather than individual host IPs — the CSV you attached is helpful. We need the final list no later than 48hrs before deploy.
2) NAT vs VPC Endpoint: we prefer NAT for outbound HTTPS unless the vendor offers an AWS PrivateLink. No PrivateLink for Splunk in our account, so NAT gateway it is.
3) Retention & PII: we need confirmation that the gateway will strip any raw PII fields before forwarding — we passed that requirement to our compliance team.

Questions:
- Can the gateway perform regex-based redaction and provide a redaction report?
- What TLS modes are supported (client certs + HMAC token)?

We can do a quick call tomorrow if that helps.

—LogisticsCorp Ops
ops@logisticscorp.com

(Attachment: sample-firewall-policy.pdf referenced)

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
To: ops@logisticscorp.com, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Oct 2028 13:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Visibility gateway runbook and egress checklist — run & review

Thanks — quick responses inline.

1) IP list: will finalize the three CIDR blocks and update the csv. We will provide a signed checksum so your network team can verify integrity.

2) NAT: fine. We'll include a note in the runbook recommending private subnets with NAT and a small route table containing only the permit rules. If you later add PrivateLink we can switch to interface endpoint; runbook will document both.

3) Redaction: the gateway supports an inline processor chain. Out of the box it can do field-level JSON redaction, regex strip, and tokenization. We will include an example redaction YAML in the runbook and a process to run a pre-flight redaction test against a sampled payload set.

4) TLS modes: HEC over mTLS is our default for Splunk; we also support TLS + HEC token. We'll add both configuration snippets to splunk-hec-config.yaml.

Action items I will take this afternoon: update the runbook with the redaction section, add the final CIDRs to network-egress-ip-list.csv, and add a bullet on KMS usage for envelope encryption.

-Laura
Laura Bennett
Manager, Customer Deployments — Redwood Inference
laura@redwood.ai

Attachment notes: will push updated files to the thread by EOD.

From: splunk-integrations@splunk.com <splunk-integrations@splunk.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>, ops@logisticscorp.com
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 19 Oct 2028 07:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Visibility gateway runbook and egress checklist — run & review

Hi Jonas / team,

Splunk team here — quick confirmation: Splunk HEC will accept mTLS client certs and token auth. For larger throughput (above ~250 req/s) we recommend HEC load balancing with multiple endpoints; please add that to the runbook if you plan for high-burst traffic.

Security note: we can also provide a scoped ingest token that expires; if LogisticsCorp wants a rotation schedule, we can automate token rotation via our API.

Happy to join the call if you need specifics on the HEC tuning parameters.

—Splunk Integrations
integrations@splunk.com

(Referenced doc: splunk-asc-quickstart.pdf)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
To: ops@logisticscorp.com, splunk-integrations@splunk.com
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 19 Oct 2028 09:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Visibility gateway runbook and egress checklist — run & review

Appreciate the quick turn. Laura, Marissa, Marcus — I incorporated Laura's updates (redaction examples and KMS note) and Splunk's guidance on HEC. Updated attachments: visibility-gateway-runbook.md (v1.1) and splunk-hec-config.yaml.

LogisticsCorp ops: can you confirm the following by EOD Monday so we can lock the window?
- Final CIDR list accepted (we added a fallback /27 if your IPs change during prep)
- Approval of pre-flight redaction test and sample dataset (we'll send a secure S3 link with sample events)

If those are a yes, I'll request the Friday 2028-10-26 maintenance window and coordinate a 60-minute rollback plan with your SRE. If there are outstanding compliance requirements I'll loop in our security team.

Jonas

Attachment stubs: visibility-gateway-runbook.md (v1.1), splunk-hec-config.yaml

From: ops@logisticscorp.com <ops@logisticscorp.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, splunk-integrations@splunk.com
Date: Mon, 22 Oct 2028 08:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Visibility gateway runbook and egress checklist — run & review

All good — LogisticsCorp approves the CIDRs in the attached CSV and the pre-flight redaction test. We reviewed the runbook with compliance; they want a short audit statement added ("redaction applied, retention policy enforced, KMS usage recorded") after the pre-flight run. Once you add that we can sign off and confirm the 2028-10-26 window.

We also request a 30-minute dry-run in our staging account on Wednesday 2028-10-24 (09:00–09:30 UTC) to validate the egress and redaction pipeline. Can you put that on the calendar?

—LogisticsCorp Ops

(Attachment: network-egress-ip-list.csv confirmed)
